name: Brahmapureeswarar Temple, Tirukkadavur Mayanam
deity: Shiva as Brahmapureeswarar, with the goddess Malarkuzhal Minnammai
period: Tevaram era (hymned 7th century); later Chola structural temple
summary: Tirukkadavur Mayanam, a cremation-ground shrine near Tirukkadaiyur, honours Shiva as Brahmapureeswarar with the goddess Malarkuzhal Minnammai. A Paadal Petra Sthalam hymned by Sambandar, Appar and Sundarar, it is one of the five Mayanam temples where the lord is said to have humbled and recreated the ego of Brahma.

sections.history: Tirukkadavur Mayanam, also Tirumayanam, lies about 1.5–3 km from the Amrita Kadeswarar temple at Tirukkadaiyur, in Mayiladuthurai district (some listings Nagapattinam). It is a Paadal Petra Sthalam, hymned in the Tevaram by Tirugnana Sambandar, Appar and Sundarar, counted among the Shiva shrines on the southern bank of the Kaveri. The stone temple is of the Chola period and later.
sections.architecture: A Dravidian delta temple, the shrine enshrines Brahmapureeswarar in the sanctum, with the goddess Malarkuzhal Minnammai — also named Nimalakuchambikai — in her own shrine, a Nandi and the parivara devatas. As a mayana koil, a cremation-ground shrine, it keeps the austere character of the five Mayanam temples; the walled courtyard is of the lower-delta form.
sections.legends: The place is a mayana koil, a cremation-ground shrine, and one of the five Mayanam temples where Shiva is said to have humbled and recreated the ego of Brahma — the others being Kachi Mayanam at Kanchipuram, Kazhi Mayanam at Sirkazhi, Naalur Mayanam, and Veezhi Mayanam at Tiruveezhimizhalai. Shiva is worshipped as Brahmapureeswarar, the lord of Brahma's city, with Malarkuzhal Minnammai beside him.
sections.festivals: The temple observes Maha Shivaratri in Masi (February–March), Navaratri in Purattasi (September–October) and the Mondays of Karthikai, with Pradosha worship. Pilgrims of the Tirukkadaiyur country, who come to the neighbouring Amrita Kadeswarar for the Markandeya legend, include this Mayanam shrine among their stops.
sections.experience: At Tirukkadavur Mayanam the pilgrim comes to a quiet cremation-ground shrine of the lower delta. Before Brahmapureeswarar and Malarkuzhal Minnammai, near Tirukkadaiyur, the visitor finds the austere grace of a Tevaram temple and the memory of Brahma's ego humbled and made new.

visit.timings: Typically open from early morning to midday and again from late afternoon into the evening; confirm timings locally, especially on festival days.
visit.dressCode: Modest traditional attire is expected, with shoulders and knees covered; footwear is left at the entrance.
visit.photography: Photography is generally allowed in the outer corridors but not inside the sanctum; ask temple staff before photographing rituals.
visit.gettingThere: Tirukkadavur Mayanam lies about 1.5–3 km from the Amrita Kadeswarar temple at Tirukkadaiyur, in Mayiladuthurai district. Tirukkadaiyur and Mayiladuthurai are the nearest towns, with buses and taxis to the shrine.
